title: Which Southland albums were made where
summary: Mares lists sessions made in the studio, at Woodman Hall, WDSU and other spots.

bands.name: Sharkey and His Kings of Dixieland

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Well, I did the Sharky with these Kings of Dixieland, and I call it the Sharky and the Jam Session in New Orleans here. That's my 205, and I made it right here in the studio. We have some live applause there, which naturally I added to it. And I've done the Monk Hazel Session in here. That's the 217. Those are the only two that I've really done in this studio.

Where were most of them done, if you don't mind telling? Well, at different spots, Bill. Any trade secrets? No, no, there's no trade, too. I mean, you know what I mean. It would be interesting for people someday to know, because on the label it doesn't tell exactly, and nobody usually tells, and they won't know unless someone like you will tell them.

Well, my 207 and Mardi Gras Parade music from New Orleans, we have things like King Zulu, and I'll Cease to Love and those tunes, and we made that at the Woodman and Royal Hall. It's a big open hall, and naturally we had to get the outside effect, and sort of an echoes outside, and we used the big hall for that. I've done probably eight or ten of them at WDSU here in New Orleans. I've used, lately I've used Dan's Pierce 600 at 501 Boybman Street, where Al Hoyt appears nightly. The acoustics are very, very fine there, and the recordings come out real good. In different spots, I used one of them at the Legion Hall, out on Canal Boulevard when I had it, and probably when I first started in 54, I made the Johnny Wiggs session there.
